title: Appeal 20538: four items for a sprinklered apartment building: balcony projections, egress-court windows, egress court roof cover, unvented roof
jurisdiction: City of Portland, Oregon (USA), Bureau of Development Services Administrative Appeal Board; non-Alberta comparative record
code_edition: 2018 IBC cited for projections; 2014 OSSC cited for item 4 (1203.2); other items edition not stated

facts.text: Item 1: balcony and porch projections toward the property lines, proposed as consistent with a 2018 IBC rule allowing 40-inch minimum projections; the record cites similar grants (appeal IDs 18056 and 20109).
Decision item 1: porch projections with a minimum 40-inch fire separation distance from the property line are granted as proposed.
Item 2: non-operable windows with sprinkler heads in an egress court less than 10 feet wide in lieu of 3/4-hour openings.

Item 2 decision: granted provided windows are non-operable, sprinklers are spaced not more than 6 feet apart and placed within specified distances of the openings, and a separate Fire Marshal permit is obtained.
Item 3: a covered 3 by 9 foot section of an egress court; decision notes the Board treated it as a partial overhead obstruction, not an open exit passageway.
Item 4: an unvented low-slope roof with continuous rigid insulation above the roof sheathing; the request says dew-point calculations are included in the submittal.
Decision item 4: unvented roof assembly is granted as proposed.
